_comment: Placeholder content overlay. The real values live in content.local.json (git-ignored). Where the library is, where the apps' checkouts are, Genau's flick words, the inbox folder a Genau flick is dropped in and the folder the toolbar's audio switch plays from are not here: they are the settings all of Haglio shares, written once in ~/.haglio/settings.json (app_support.haglio_settings). pinned_kino_settings is optional as well: an action named here pins the gallery's Combine to this hand-tuned workflow+params (any param unnamed falls to the workflow's defaults, seeds are re-rolled per launch) instead of taking settings from past videos — the way out when an action's past videos all share a weakness. pinned_genau_settings is the same table for Combine's Genau lane, which makes one looping cycle rather than a full-length video: the key is the action again, so the two tables are separate — one keyed by action alone could hold an action's long-form settings or its loop's, never both. Both are optional, and an action missing from one is mined from past videos instead (for the Genau lane, only from videos a looping workflow made). detail_fix_parts is optional: extra parts the spoken "fix <part>" command can aim the enhance's detail pass at, beyond the built-in faces/hands/teeth/eyes — name is the word captions use, spoken the words the command may say, matches the filename substrings that recognize an installed detector (under ComfyUI's models/ultralytics/bbox) as finding it, and shared_photos false trains the part's LoRA on its own folder of images alone, never on the fixes folder's shared one. search_synonyms is optional: extra groups of interchangeable words for the gallery search, each group a list of single words that all satisfy a query for any other — the built-in table in origenerator/search.py is general English, so vocabulary describing the library itself goes here. A group sharing a word with a built-in group extends it rather than replacing it; multi-word entries are ignored, since matching is word by word. speech_python is optional: the full path of the Python interpreter of the environment Qwen3-TTS is installed in (the app runs origenerator/speech_worker.py under it to speak a story's scene lines); omit it and a run with lines fails at submit saying no voice is set up. video_actions.starts_from says which animations are worth asking for: per lane (video, the full-length clip, and genau, the single looping cycle), per video button, the image buttons an animation of it can sensibly start from; a checkbox of the video buttons' own makes an animation of its own with each of them, from the same images. A button missing from a lane can be asked for from no image at all, and an image button missing from a button's list answers a command naming it by saying so rather than animating something that cannot work. model_recommendations is what each checkpoint file's own page recommends, keyed by the file's name: the model's name as the page gives it, the samplers it names (each with the step spacings it pairs that sampler with, or none when it names none), steps and cfg as [lowest, highest], and the start a fresh form takes on that model; lora_recommendations is the same for a LoRA file, with strength, cfg, steps and shift. A setting outside what a page recommends wears a warning that quotes the page's name. krea2_training_python and krea2_training_scripts are optional: the Python of the environment musubi-tuner is installed in and the musubi-tuner folder, which train a look LoRA on Krea 2 (origenerator/look_training.py runs tools/look_lora_trainer.py under it); omit them and a Train press for a look LoRA says no training program is set up. trainable_loras is optional: the LoRAs Origenerator can train a next version of, keyed by the title base every version of one shares (a title is the base and a version, as in "Example Look 1.0"), each with the folder of images it is trained on and the Krea 2 Raw model, text encoder and VAE files, under ComfyUI's diffusion_models, text_encoders and vae folders, it is trained with, and optionally trigger_words, the words its next version is trained to answer to ([] for none; without the key, the newest version's recorded words). image_actions and video_actions are the action setter tool's for images and for videos: buttons maps each button, in the order the tool lays them out, to the actions a press saves on the item; grid arranges the buttons the way picture_state_grid arranges the states; checkboxes are the boxes above the buttons, each saved by name on the item when checked; formerly maps a name an item was answered with before to the actions and checked boxes it now means, so the answers given before the buttons changed carry over; drawn_as names the drawing a button wears when it is not the button's own name. site_words maps each word another site gives a video it made (the words its record keeps, and the Random Faves Browser sends back to that site) to the labels it means, on the video and on its starting frame: a word may stand after another word that is in the table too, as a camera word does, and a word that means nothing leaves the video for the action setter tool.

params.positive_prompt: third box form, an example scene unfolds
beta form, one complete example motion, returning to where it began

genau_flick_prompts.positive: (one complete alpha cycle: all the way out, then all the way in, then return:1.5), (long travel:1.4)

beta.positive: (one complete beta cycle: all the way down, then all the way up, then return:1.5), (long travel:1.4)
